Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Eileen Lopez and Monica Garcia.

The Invocation was led by Chaplain Elvin Miranda, Azusa Police Department.

City Attorney Richman reported that four items were discussed in Closed Session and that there was no
reportable action.

CEREMONIAL

Recognition of the Azusa High School Varsity Boys Basketball Team.

Councilmember Mendez recognized the Azusa High School varsity basketball team for their achievement as
finalists in the CIF Championship.

Recognition of the Azusa High School Academic Decathlon Team.

Councilmember Bow recognized members of the Azusa High School Academic Decathlon team for placing
first for most improved score and earning second place in the Super Quiz, Division 3.

Presentation of a proclamation declaring April 2026 as Donate Life Month in the City of Azusa.

Councilmember Bow presented a proclamation declaring April 2026 as Donate Life Month in the City of
Azusa.

Presentation of a proclamation declaring April 10 as Arbor Day in the City of Azusa.

Mayor Alvarez presented a proclamation declaring April 10, 2026, as Arbor Day in the City of Azusa, which
was accepted by Director of Public Works Robert Delgadillo.

Presentation of proclamations in honor of Earth Day 2026: City’s Clean and Green Month and Recycling and
Recycling and Organics Separation Month

Mayor Pro Tem Avila presented a proclamation declaring April 2026 as Clean and Green Month in the City of
Azusa.

Councilmember Gonzales presented a proclamation declaring April 2026 as Recycling and Organic Separation
Month in honor of Earth Day 2026 on behalf Senator Rubio.

A representative from Athens Services, Denay Amaya, spoke about the importance of source separation and

April 6, 2026
 highlighted the successful compost and mulch giveaway event.

Presentation of a proclamation declaring April 2026 as Autism Awareness Month in the City of Azusa.

Mayor Pro Tem Avila presented a proclamation declaring April 2026 as Autism Awareness Month in the City
of Azusa, which was received by Ambassador Eliza Rietta.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

Venerable Nicholas Thanissaro from the Dhammakaya Meditation Center invited the community to attend the
first outdoor candlelight meditation event of the year on April 18.

Dr. Marisol Martinez-Garcia, Board Member of Faith Family Center, introduced the new church to the Azusa
community, located at 405 South Azusa Avenue, and invited all to visit.

Damaris Flores, a resident, shared her thoughts on Faith Family Center joining the Azusa community and
highlighted the various events and activities the church offers.

REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

City Manager Communications

City Manager Gonzalez provided two announcements; that with the approval of street closures, the City will
host another Night Market on April 16; and the State of the City event will be held on May 6.

Councilmember Announcements

Mayor Pro Tem Avila announced several City events, including: Family Craft Hour at the Azusa City Library
on April 14, Azusa Shred-A-Thon on April 18 at the Azusa Light & Water parking lot, and Senior Talent Show
on April 30 at the Azusa North Recreation Center; shared that the Azusa Golden Days Committee will host a
golf tournament on May 29; and extended farewell wishes to Pastor Will from Sandals Church as he departs
Azusa to launch a new Sandals Church in Anaheim.

Councilmember Mendez announced the following City events: Outdoor Recreation and Eco Fair on April 10,
Family Game Night on April 17 at the Azusa City Library, and E-Waste Collection on April 18 at the Public
Works Yard.

Councilmember Bow announced the return of the Azusa Night Market during the months of April, May, and
June; and reported attending the Water Education for Latino Leaders (WELL) conference in Northern
California on March 27–28.

Councilmember Gonzales announced the following upcoming City events: Senior Services Social Seminar on
April 9 at the North Recreation Center, and free tire disposal available April 1–30 at Waste Management
facility.

Mayor Alvarez announced upcoming events at the Azusa City Library: Dia de los Niños (Children’s Day) on
April 21, followed by an Earth Day “Dirt Cup” activity on April 23; reported his attendance at a Foothill Transit
meeting, where discussions included the anticipated need for additional buses during the upcoming Olympics
and Paralympics, stated that the City is currently awaiting determination on whether federal funding will be
provided to support these transit needs; and noted his attendance at Gladstone Middle School’s performance of
Rock of Ages.

SCHEDULED ITEMS

PUBLIC HEARING – AB 2561 LOCAL PUBLIC EMPLOYEES: VACANT POSITIONS

Director of Administrative Services Johnson introduced the item stating that an annual update is required
pursuant to Assembly Bill No. 2561; and introduced Payroll and Acting Human Resources Supervisor
Rodriguez, who presented the update.

City Council Minutes  Page | 3
April 6, 2026
 Acting Human Resources Supervisor Rodriguez gave an overview of AB 2561; reported that as of February 1,
2026, the City has 378 budgeted full-time positions, with 288 positions represented across eight bargaining
groups; presented data on union-represented vacancies, including those within the Azusa Mid-Management
Association and Azusa Police Executive groups, and discussed potential recruitment obstacles; reviewed
recruitment and selection efforts and provided a personnel action report, noting an increase in active employees
from 384 in January 2025 to 415 in December 2025; and emphasized the City’s key priorities of recruitment,
retention, and operational efficiency to maintain service levels and workforce stability.

Councilmembers asked questions regarding candidate drop-off during recruitment. Staff explained that
candidates often withdraw due to accepting other positions or higher compensation elsewhere, though specific
reasons are not always communicated. The Council also inquired why the presentation had not been provided
prior to budget adoption. Staff clarified that a presentation was given in April, but it was less detailed because
no bargaining groups exceeded the 20% vacancy threshold at that time.

Additional questions were raised regarding responsibility for reviewing vacancy data. Staff responded that
Human Resources would oversee the review in coordination with the bargaining groups.

Mayor Alvarez opened the Public Hearing.

City Clerk Cornejo certified the publication of the Public Hearing in the San Gabriel Valley Tribune on March
16, 2026.

Public Comment

Kevin Norton, a representative from IBEW Local 18, addressed the Council, stating that the organization
represents employees from Azusa Light and Water; recommended that the Council, in coordination with Human
Resources, review Los Angeles County utility salary benchmarks, noting the highly competitive nature of the
industry.

City Clerk Cornejo confirmed that no additional speaker cards were received.

Moved by Councilmember Gonzales, seconded by Councilmember Mendez and carried unanimously by the
following roll call vote of the Council to close the Public Hearing.

AYES: ALVAREZ, AVILA, GONZALES, MENDEZ, BOW
NOES: NONE

TWILIGHT BICYCLE RACE TO BE HELD ON JULY 11, 2026, WAIVE SPECIAL EVENT PERMIT
APPLICATION FEES, AND ADOPT A RESOLUTION TO ALLOW FOR STREET CLOSURES THE
DAY OF THE EVENT

Director of Economic and Community Development Jimenez presented an item for consideration to co-sponsor
a criterium bike race scheduled for July 11, 2026. The proposal included waiving special event permit
application fees and adopting a resolution to allow temporary street closures for the duration of the event; and
explained that the race would require two street closures and would be conducted on a one-kilometer closed
circuit.

Patrick Caro, of Go Fast-Andiamo, introduced himself and stated that he organizes bicycle races throughout
Southern California. In response to Council inquiries, Caro indicated that he anticipates approximately 300 to
400 cyclists will participate in the event.

The Council discussed the potential costs associated with hosting the event. Staff indicated that a more detailed
cost estimate will be presented at a future meeting but provided a preliminary estimate ranging from $6,000 to

April 6, 2026
 $10,000. Staff also noted that hosting the event would create an opportunity to support and promote business
activity at local shops.

Moved by Councilmember Gonzales, seconded by Councilmember Mendez and carried by the following vote
of the Council, to authorize and adopt Resolution No. 2026 – C16 to allow for the temporary street closure and
use of the public right-of way on Azusa Avenue between 5th Street and Santa Fe Avenue, San Gabriel Avenue
between 6th Street and the southernmost point of the Metro/Heavy Rail lines, and Foothill Blvd between
Angeleno Avenue and Dalton Avenue for Twilight Criterium Bicycle Race and activities; authorize the City
Manager to execute the Special Event Permit Agreement with Go Fast-Andiamo of Twilight Criterium Bicycle
Race, in a form acceptable to the City Attorney, on behalf of the City; and make a finding that the community at
large will receive public benefits with the co-sponsorship by the City and waiving of associated event costs.

CONSIDERATION TO ADOPT A RESOLUTION TO ALLOW FOR LIMITED STREET CLOSURES
FOR THE DOWNTOWN AZUSA NIGHT MARKET SERIES TAKING PLACE ON THE THIRD
THURSDAY OF THE YEAR DURING 2026

Management Analyst Nazarian, from the City Manager’s Office, requested City Council authorization for
limited street closures to accommodate the Azusa Downtown Night Market series, proposed to take place on the
third Thursday of each month through 2026; noted that the City will partner with Angel City Market on a trial
basis to deliver a larger and enhanced event experience, with the first event scheduled for April 16, 2026.

Councilmembers inquired about the placement of vendor canopies and whether they would obstruct existing
businesses. Staff responded that, in accordance with Los Angeles County Fire Department guidelines, canopies
will be positioned along the outer edges of the street to maintain a required 20-foot fire lane.

Additional discussion addressed the selection of Thursdays as the designated event day. Staff explained that
neighboring cities typically host similar events on Fridays, and scheduling the market on Thursdays avoids
competition while allowing City Staff to be readily available on-site to provide support.

Moved by Councilmember Gonzales, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Avila and carried by the following vote of
the Council, to authorize and adopt Resolution No.2026 – C17 to allow for the temporary street closure and use
of the public right-of way on Azusa Ave between 6th St. And Foothill Blvd. for the Azusa Night Market Series.

CONSIDERATION OF FISCAL YEAR 2025-26 MID-YEAR BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS AND FISCAL
YEAR 2026-27 MID-CYCLE BUDGET REVIEW

Director of Administrative Services Johnson introduced Item D-4 regarding the Fiscal Year 2025–26 mid-year
budget adjustments and the Fiscal Year 2026–27 mid-cycle budget review; noted that no changes to the overall
budget amounts were being recommended at this time; rather, the presentation was intended to provide high-
level information to assist with the adoption of the Fiscal Year 2027 budget in June.

Johnson delivered a three-part presentation, which included: recommended adjustments to the Fiscal Year
2025–26 budget, a high-level overview of budget considerations, and a snapshot of the General Fund’s fiscal
position; explained that by the end of the current fiscal year, the City is projected to have total ending reserves
of just under $58 million.

April 6, 2026
 Council and Staff engaged in discussion regarding the overall budget outlook. Staff highlighted that strong sales
tax performance is expected to contribute to continued financial progress; noted that while the City is currently
in a strong cash position, a cautious approach is being maintained with respect to year-to-year budgeting. With
continued prudent spending, the City is estimated to have access to approximately $19 million beyond the
designated reserve.

Moved by Councilmember Bow, seconded by Councilmember Mendez and carried by the following vote of the
Council, to adopt Resolution No. 2026-C19 approving the Fiscal Year 2025/26 mid-year budget adjustments;
receive, review, and file the Fiscal Year 2025/26 Second Quarter Budget-to-Actual financial report; and provide
input and direction on key considerations for the Fiscal Year 2026/27 budget in advance of adoption in June
2026.
